blocks.content: Explore a heatmap to see how each cell combines a time bucket, a numeric range, and a count.
Open **Grafana Heatmaps** and keep the full dashboard visible.
Find the **Linear** heatmap near **Random Timeseries Data**. Read time on the horizontal axis and numeric value ranges on the vertical axis.

Use the color legend to identify which colors represent higher counts. Hover over a cell and read its time, value bucket, and count. The cell's vertical position isn't its count; color encodes the count.

Follow a band of occupied cells from an earlier time to a later time. Notice whether the observations stay in similar value ranges or move higher or lower. This adds the timing that a single histogram leaves out.
A heatmap answers "How does the distribution change over time?" Read the legend rather than assuming darker or redder always means more. These are numeric buckets, not healthy or unhealthy states.
You've read time, numeric ranges, and counts together. Next, switch from numeric distributions to discrete states.
